home.meta-title: Passport and Visa Photo Maker — Free, Private, In Your Browser
home.meta-description: Make a compliant passport or visa photo for free. Correct head height, eye line and background for each country, plus a printable 4x6 sheet. Nothing is uploaded.
home.title: Passport and visa photos that actually meet the requirements
home.subtitle: Most rejected photos fail on head size, not on the crop. Pick a document below and this tool measures your face, positions it inside the permitted range, replaces the background and gives you a printable sheet.
home.privacy: Every step runs inside your browser. Your photo is never uploaded, never stored and never seen by anyone but you.
home.how-p1: Every authority publishes two numbers that matter more than the outer size: how tall your head must be from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head, and sometimes how far your eyes must sit above the bottom edge. These are narrow ranges, often only five millimetres wide, and a crop that looks right by eye lands outside them more often than not.
home.how-p2: Head height is measured to the top of the head {em}including hair{/em}, which is why this tool separates you from the background first: the outline of your hair is what reveals where the top of your head really is. Face-detection models stop at the hairline and consistently underestimate it. Once the crown, chin and eye line are known, the crop is computed to land in the middle of each permitted range rather than at its edge, which leaves the most room for error.
home.how-p2__note: {em} and {/em} mark where an emphasised phrase starts and ends; it renders in italics. Keep the pair, keep them in that order, and put them around whichever words carry the emphasis in your language.
home.how-p3: If your original photo is framed too tightly to produce a compliant result, the tool says which edge falls short instead of cropping in further and handing you something that will be turned down at the counter.

about.meta-description: Why this tool exists, how it measures head height from the hair rather than the hairline, and why every photograph is processed on your own device.
about.title: About
about.why-p1: Passport photo rejections are mostly one problem wearing different hats: the head is the wrong size. Authorities publish a narrow permitted range — often a five millimetre window on a forty-five millimetre photo — and there is no way to hit it reliably by cropping to the right outer dimensions and hoping. Meanwhile most free tools want you to upload a photograph of your face to a server you know nothing about, and most paid ones charge for a crop.
about.why-p2: This tool does the measurement properly and does it on your own machine.
about.measures-p1: Every specification measures head height from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head {em}including hair{/em}. That last part is the hard part. Face-landmark models — the standard tool for finding features in a photograph — have no landmark for the top of the skull; their highest point sits around the hairline, so any estimate built from them is systematically short, and short in exactly the dimension that gets photos rejected.
about.measures-p1__note: {em} and {/em} mark where an emphasised phrase starts and ends; it renders in italics. Keep the pair, keep them in that order, and put them around whichever words carry the emphasis in your language.
about.measures-p2: So the pipeline runs in an order that might look backwards: it separates you from the background first, then reads the top of your head off the outline of your hair, and only uses the landmark model for the chin and the eye line. The background separation was needed anyway to replace the background with the required colour, so the accurate measurement comes free.
about.measures-p3: With the crown, chin and eye line known, the crop is computed to land in the middle of every permitted range rather than near an edge, which leaves the widest margin for the small errors any automatic measurement makes. If your original photograph is framed too tightly for a compliant crop to exist, the tool tells you which edge is short instead of cropping further and producing something that will fail.
about.upload-p1: A passport photograph is a picture of your face attached to an identity document application. There is no good reason for it to travel to someone else's server to be cropped, and several bad ones. Face detection, background separation, cropping and JPEG encoding all run in your browser through WebAssembly. You can confirm it in the Network tab of your browser's developer tools.
about.honest-heading: How the specifications are kept honest
about.honest-p1: Each page links the official source its numbers came from and shows the date a person last read that source. A specification that has not been checked against its source does not get published at all — the build skips it — because a confidently wrong page here costs someone a rejected application. There are currently {count} verified specifications on the site.
about.honest-p1__note: {count} is how many verified specifications the site publishes in this language, already written as a number for it. Nothing else is substituted, so put whatever words the sentence needs around it.
about.honest-p2: If you spot a number that no longer matches the official page, that is the most useful thing you can tell us.
about.paid-p1: Advertising covers hosting. The tool itself is free, has no account, no usage limit and no paid tier, and advertisers receive nothing about you from us beyond what Google's own advertising systems collect. They never receive your photograph, because we never have a copy of it.
privacy.meta-description: How this site handles your data. Photos are processed entirely in your browser and never uploaded. This page explains what is and is not collected.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.photos-p1: Photographs you open in this tool are never uploaded. Face detection, background separation, cropping and encoding all run inside your own browser using WebAssembly. No copy of your image is transmitted to this site's servers or to any third party, and no copy is stored anywhere after you close or reload the page.
privacy.photos-p2: This is a property of how the tool is built, not a policy promise we ask you to take on trust. You can verify it: open your browser's developer tools, switch to the Network tab, and process a photo. You will see requests for the model files and nothing carrying your image.
privacy.collected-p1: We do not ask you to create an account and we do not collect names, email addresses or any other personal details. Standard server logs may record the IP address, browser user agent and requested URL of visits, which is unavoidable in serving a website and is used only to keep the site running and to diagnose faults.
privacy.ads-p1: This site displays advertising supplied by Google, which pays for its hosting. Google and its partners may set cookies or read existing ones to serve and measure ads, and may use your approximate location and browsing history to choose which ads to show. This happens through Google's advertising systems; we never pass your photograph or any image data to them, because we never have a copy to pass on.
privacy.ads-p2: If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, you will be asked for consent before any non-essential cookie is set, and you can change or withdraw that choice at any time. You can also review and adjust the ads you see at {a1}Google My Ad Center{/a1}, and opt out of personalised advertising from participating vendors at {a2}aboutads.info{/a2}.
privacy.ads-p2__note: {a1} and {/a1} wrap the words that link to Google My Ad Center, and {a2} and {/a2} wrap the words that link to aboutads.info. The two addresses come from the page and are never read from this file, so keep each pair around the words naming that destination, keep both members of a pair, and move the pairs wherever your sentence needs them.
privacy.rights-p1: Because we hold no account and no photographs, there is normally no personal data of yours for us to show you, correct or delete. If you believe we hold something about you and want it removed, contact us and we will act on it.
privacy.children-p1: This site is not directed at children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect information from them. A parent making a passport photo for a child is of course welcome to use the tool; the photograph stays on their device like any other.
privacy.changes-p1: If this policy changes, the date at the top of this page changes with it. Material changes will be noted on the site.
terms.meta-description: The terms covering use of this passport photo tool, including what it does, what it cannot guarantee, and the limits of our liability.
terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.provides-p1: This site provides a free tool that crops and formats a photograph to the published specification for a passport, visa or similar document, and summarises those published specifications. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or acting on behalf of any government, passport authority, embassy or consulate.
terms.accuracy-heading: Accuracy, and what we cannot promise
terms.accuracy-p1: The measurements on each page are transcribed from the official source linked at the bottom of that page, and each carries the date a person last checked it. Requirements do change, and specifications are sometimes interpreted differently by different offices handling the same application.
terms.accuracy-p2: We therefore cannot guarantee that a photograph produced here will be accepted. The tool reports whether the output meets the measurements we hold on file; acceptance is the decision of the authority receiving your application, and factors it judges by eye — expression, lighting, shadows on your face, whether your hair covers your eyes — are outside what any automated check can confirm. Always read the authority's own page before you submit, and treat the linked source as authoritative over this site.
terms.use-p1: Use the tool for your own photographs, or for photographs you have permission to process. Do not use it to produce images intended to misrepresent someone's identity, and do not attempt to interfere with the site's operation or with other visitors' use of it.
terms.liability-p1: The tool is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. To the fullest extent the law allows, we are not liable for any loss arising from use of this site, including a rejected application, a missed appointment, a delayed trip, or fees you paid to an authority. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited.
terms.ip-p1: The text, design and code of this site belong to its operator. Your photographs remain entirely yours; we neither receive nor claim any rights in them.
terms.changes-p1: These terms may be updated, and the date above will change when they are. Continuing to use the site after a change means you accept the revised terms.

spec.caption: {documentName} requirements
spec.caption__note: Screen-reader caption of the requirements table. {documentName} is the spec's own document name, e.g. US passport photo.
spec.dimensions__note: A photo size, used on its own on the home page and inside spec.size-print. {width} and {height} are numbers already formatted for this locale; {unit} is the value of unit.mm or unit.px.
spec.size-print__note: {physical} and {pixels} are complete phrases already built from spec.dimensions — 50.8 × 50.8 mm and 600 × 600 px — not bare numbers. {dpi} is a number and {dpiUnit} is the value of unit.dpi.
spec.band-length__note: A permitted range in the units an authority publishes. {minLength} and {maxLength} are numbers with one decimal and {unit} is the value of unit.mm. {minPercent} and {maxPercent} already include the % sign, so adding another gives 50%%.
spec.band-percent__note: The same range for a spec that states pixels only and has no print size. {minPercent} and {maxPercent} already include the % sign.
spec.file-max__note: Shown when an authority caps the file size. {size} is a number, {unit} is the value of unit.kb.
spec.file-min__note: Shown when an authority sets a floor on the file size. {size} is a number, {unit} is the value of unit.kb.
spec.file-separator__note: Joins the file constraints into one table cell: JPEG, max 240 KB. Include whatever spaces the language needs, and never leave it empty or the values run together.
schema.app-name__note: The application name in the page's structured data, read by search engines rather than shown on the page. {documentName} is the spec's own document name.
